chunks: Ibn Mahbūb narrated from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who accused his wife of zinā while she was mute and deaf, not hearing what he said. He said: "If she has evidence—witnesses who testify for her before the Imam—he is flogged with the legal punishment, and the two are separated; then she is never lawful for him again. But if she has no evidence, then she is forbidden to him so long as he remains with her, and there is no sin upon her from him."

key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidence, especially supporting witnesses
key_terms.قَذَفَ: he made a slanderous accusation of zinā
key_terms.ٱلزِّنَا: illicit sexual intercourse; the offense being alleged
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the judicial authority before whom the matter is established

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man accuses his mute and deaf wife of adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a husband who accuses his wife of zinā when she is unable to hear or respond because she is mute and deaf. It explains the judicial role of proof before the Imam and the consequences of either establishing or failing to establish evidence, including hadd punishment, separation, and the woman's lack of sin in the matter.
